title: Culture, Conduct and Speaking Up
summary: How tone from the top, incentives and the board's own behaviour shape whether staff report concerns and whether commercial pressure overrides financial crime controls.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How tone from the top, incentives and the board's own behaviour shape whether staff report concerns and whether commercial pressure overrides financial crime controls.
Learning Objectives: Assess the firm's financial crime culture and the signals the board sends
Evaluate whether incentives and commercial pressure undermine controls
Identify how the board oversees whistleblowing and speaking up
Syllabus: Tone from the top, the middle and the front line
Remuneration, sales incentives and accountability for breaches
Whistleblowing arrangements and the board's champion
Training and awareness that changes behaviour
Intended Audience: Chairs, non-executive and independent directors and board committee members, especially on risk and audit committees
Executive directors and senior managers accountable for financial crime, compliance and operations
Company secretaries and heads of governance supporting board oversight
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board or senior management experience in financial services is helpful. No specialist background in financial crime compliance is required.
Core Reading: FATF, International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations (as updated)
Basel Committee, Corporate Governance Principles for Banks (2015)
